profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting at a hospital-affiliated cardiovascular research center to organize the final webinar session in an internal 4-part education series for investigators and coordinators, titled 'Challenging Issues in Clinical Trial Design: Part 4.' The session will use the cardiology-focused paper as the anchor reading and is intended for fellows, research nurses, junior faculty, and trial coordinators preparing for upcoming investigator-initiated studies. The agenda is to decide the structure of the 75-minute session, assign preparation tasks, determine what pre-read and case materials will be circulated, and confirm what operational approvals are needed before invitations go out. The expected outcome is a shared plan for content, logistics, responsibilities, and timing for a session scheduled two weeks from now.

members.name: Dr. Maya Srinivasan
members.role: Associate Director of Cardiovascular Clinical Trials Education
members.expertise: Cardiology trial methodology, investigator training, and protocol development
members.background: An interventional cardiologist who now leads faculty education for the center's clinical research office; she has chaired several investigator meetings and often frames teaching sessions around design concepts and landmark examples.
members.private_state: She wants the session to feel academically rigorous and reusable as a model for future teaching, while keeping faculty effort low enough that senior investigators will continue participating in the series.
hidden_assumptions: When a session is described as 'case-based,' it mainly needs concise slide-based summaries of published cardiology trials rather than fully worked participant exercises.
Sending the 'reading packet' means distributing the focal paper plus 1-2 optional landmark articles, since learners in this series are used to selective pre-reading rather than a comprehensive pack.
A 'finalized agenda' for an education session means the teaching flow, timings, and faculty ownership are settled, even if room-level operations and CME-style documentation are completed afterward.
For a session on DMCs and adaptive designs, institutional review is not needed unless actual unpublished internal trial data or patient-level materials are being shown.

members.name: Elena Morales
members.expertise: Research program logistics, educational event coordination, compliance workflows, and coordinator training
members.background: She oversees operational support for the cardiovascular trials unit, including seminar scheduling, materials distribution, attendance tracking, and coordination with compliance and education offices.
members.private_state: She wants to avoid last-minute operational risk and make sure the event can be executed smoothly with materials that coordinators can directly use afterward.
hidden_assumptions: When faculty ask for a 'case-based' session, attendees usually expect a practical worksheet or discussion prompt built around trial scenarios they can actively work through in small groups.
A 'reading packet' normally includes all participant-facing materials in one distribution bundle: article, glossary, discussion questions, and any trial summary handout.
An agenda is not really 'final' until invitations, room setup, attendance process, and any compliance-sensitive review steps are locked, because those pieces drive the actual event launch.

Using examples about stopping early, DMC decisions, or adaptive modifications can trigger a quick compliance or communications check if examples are drawn from the center's ongoing studies, even when no raw data are shared.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as a case-based format
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the session should be 'case-based.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a faculty-led presentation built around a few brief slide summaries of published cardiology trials illustrating noninferiority, factorial, strategy, DMC, and adaptive design issues.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means participants will receive at least one structured scenario or worksheet to discuss in breakout-style or guided interactive segments.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In medical education meetings, 'case-based' is a positively valenced, familiar phrase that often goes unexamined because both a slide vignette and an interactive exercise plausibly fit the label.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the reading packet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss sending out the 'reading packet' by next Wednesday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means the anchor paper and perhaps a couple of optional landmark trial PDFs or citations.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means the full participant bundle, including article PDF, one-page glossary, discussion prompts, and any case handout attendees need for the session.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are accustomed to educational events where materials are circulated in advance, and 'packet' sounds concrete enough that neither expects the boundary of included items to need explicit negotiation.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They aim to have the 'agenda finalized' by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the criterion is that the instructional sequence, speakers, and time allocations are set so she can stop revising the academic content.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the agenda is only final when it is ready for operational release, meaning timings, format details, room setup implications, invitation text, and attendance/compliance workflow are all settled.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'finalized agenda' is routine in planning conversations and usually signals progress rather than a specific checklist, so each person silently maps it onto the standards used in their own function.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They mention possibly using the Riverside antithrombotic study as one of the examples.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes that if the example is discussed only at a high level and framed around published-like design issues, no extra review is needed before inclusion.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes that because Riverside is an active local study, even a teaching mention tied to stopping rules or adaptations should be run through a quick compliance/communications check before materials are distributed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each treats their background rule as already institutional common sense, and because neither is proposing anything obviously risky, the mention passes as a minor logistical detail rather than a point requiring clarification.

turns.inner_thought: This last session should feel stronger than the earlier ones without becoming labor-intensive. If I anchor it in the cardiology paper and frame it as case-based, I can use concise slide vignettes from a few landmark trials and keep the faculty contribution manageable. That also gives us something polished enough to reuse next year.
turns.utterance: Thanks for making time, Elena. For Part 4, I'd like us to build the 75-minute session around the cardiology paper and make it more case-based than the earlier sessions.

turns.inner_thought: Good—if it's case-based, people will expect something they can actually work through, not just another webinar with examples on slides. Coordinators and fellows usually engage better when they leave with a practical tool or scenario they can use afterward. Two weeks is tight but still workable if we lock deliverables early.
turns.utterance: I think that makes sense. If we do it that way, it should leave the coordinators and fellows with something practical they can use after the discussion, and the date two weeks from now is still realistic from my side.

turns.inner_thought: I'll keep the flow clean and faculty-led: brief sections that move from classic design choices into the harder judgment calls. Published cardiology examples will do the teaching efficiently without forcing us to build elaborate exercises.
turns.utterance: My thought for the flow is to open with short segments on noninferiority, then factorial and strategy trials, and then spend the back half on DMCs, early stopping, and adaptive designs using cardiology examples.

turns.inner_thought: That sequence is workable operationally. I need the reading packet out by next Wednesday if people are supposed to come prepared for the discussion materials. For me that packet means the whole participant bundle, not just articles, because the prompts and handouts shape how I set expectations in the invitation.
turns.utterance: That structure works for me. Could we plan on sending out the reading packet by next Wednesday so attendees have enough time to prepare?

turns.inner_thought: Yes, I can easily send the anchor paper and one or two landmark trial pieces by then. That is already more pre-reading than many of them will finish, and I don't want to overload busy clinicians before a noon session.
turns.utterance: Yes, I can do that. I'll send the paper and a couple of landmark trial pieces; that should be enough pre-reading for this audience.

turns.inner_thought: Great, once I have everything for the packet, I'll bundle the article with the glossary, prompts, and the case handout so participants have one clean set of materials. If they're going to use those discussion prompts live, I need formatting time and probably a final version before invitation copy goes out.
turns.utterance: Perfect. Once the reading packet is assembled, I can format it for distribution and make sure it lines up with the discussion prompts attendees will use during the session.

turns.inner_thought: Riverside would be a strong local example because everyone knows the study name and it illustrates exactly the kind of stopping-rule and adaptation questions I want to highlight. If I keep it at the level of design principles and avoid unpublished details, I don't see that as needing extra institutional review.
turns.utterance: One possibility is to use the Riverside antithrombotic study as one of the examples when we get to stopping decisions and adaptive modifications, since people will immediately recognize the context.

turns.inner_thought: That could be a very effective example, but because Riverside is active and local, I want a quick compliance or communications check before anything participant-facing goes out. Even high-level references can trigger questions if they're tied to stopping or adaptation language.
turns.utterance: I agree, that could be a strong example. I'll make sure anything tied to Riverside is cleared before the materials go out.

turns.inner_thought: I need the agenda finalized by Friday in the academic sense: sequence, timings, and who owns which segment. If that is set, I can stop revising the content and ask the discussants for their slides without dragging this into another week.
turns.utterance: I would like to have the agenda finalized by Friday so I can lock the teaching flow and ask the faculty discussants for their slides.

turns.inner_thought: Friday works if 'finalized' really means I can launch from it—invitation text, room setup, attendance tracking, and any review steps all depend on those details not moving afterward. If I tell my team it's final, I need it to be operationally release-ready.
turns.utterance: Friday is workable. Once the agenda is finalized, I can release the invitations, confirm the room setup, and close the attendance workflow.

turns.inner_thought: I'll keep ownership clear: I should handle the intellectual architecture and select the trials, while Elena manages circulation and execution. That division usually keeps faculty from getting bogged down in logistics.
turns.utterance: Why don't I take the first pass at the session outline and choose the cardiology trial examples, and you can handle circulation and the event logistics?

turns.inner_thought: That division is fine, as long as I receive enough material to build the full packet and launch the event cleanly. I'll plan to package all participant-facing documents, get the Riverside check done, and be ready for the case-based session once Friday's version is truly final from an operations standpoint.
turns.utterance: That works. I'll package the materials, check the Riverside-related approvals, and get everything ready for the case-based session once Friday's agenda is final.
